title: Hooke’s Law: Stress and Strain Revisited
lead: An object that is pushed away from its equilibrium position and let go will oscillate if a force pulls it back. This section describes the simplest such force, one that is proportional to the displacement, and shows how much energy a deformed object stores.
objectives: Explain Newton’s third law of motion with respect to stress and deformation.
Describe the restoration of force and displacement.
Calculate the energy in Hooke’s Law of deformation, and the stored energy in a spring.
summary_html:
• An oscillation is a back and forth motion of an object between two points of deformation.
  • An oscillation may create a wave, which is a disturbance that propagates from where it was created.
  • The simplest type of oscillations and waves are related to systems that can be described by Hooke’s law: $\kF = -\kk\kx,$ where $\kF$ is the restoring force, $\kx$ is the displacement from equilibrium or deformation, and $\kk$ is the force constant of the system.
  • Elastic potential energy $\kPE$ stored in the deformation of a system that can be described by Hooke’s law is given by $\kPE = (1/2)\kk\kx^2.$
